subject: Model triage + runtime runway for ClearLedger onboarding
messages:
From: aditya_rao@redwood.example.com
To: Ethan Cho <ethan@clearledger.com>, Priya Shah <priya.ops@clearledger.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.example.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.example.com>
Date: 2026-11-22T10:12:00-08:00
Subject: Model triage + runtime runway for ClearLedger onboarding

Ethan / Priya — thanks again for the call this morning. To prep the onboarding kickoff next week CS/Eng asked me to capture a short model triage and estimated runtime runway so we can lock the initial slot on Dedicated. Quick asks to unblock our engineering planning: 

1) Clarify peak vs steady QPS and typical payload sizes (avg prompt tokens, avg response tokens). If you can share a short CSV with per-endpoint samples that’s ideal.
2) Confirm the maximum required context length for the two main features: (a) transaction reconciliation assistant and (b) policy QA.
3) Any strict PII retention constraints or redaction rules that would affect caching/kv-cache (we recommend prefix caching for repeated prefixes).

We’ll produce a short shortlist (3 model variants), a recommended quantization/latency profile, and an hourly token runway that maps to Dedicated pool sizing. I’m attaching a template CSV to make the token profile quick.

Next steps: if you can drop the CSV by EOD Tue we’ll circulate a proposed shortlist + cost/latency tradeoffs by Wed and can lock the Dedicated slot by Friday.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Sr. Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.example.com
Redwood Inference

From: Ethan Cho <ethan@clearledger.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.example.com
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.ops@clearledger.com>
Date: 2026-11-22T14:06:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Model triage + runtime runway for ClearLedger onboarding

Aditya — attaching the exports as requested. We included two endpoints: /reconcile and /policy-check. Quick summary first:

- Steady: 12 requests/min across both endpoints (avg 0.2s inter-arrival per user peak). Peak burst observed during statement uploads: up to 75 req/min for ~20 minutes.
- Average prompt size: /reconcile 420 tokens, /policy-check 130 tokens. Average response size: /reconcile 520 tokens, /policy-check 260 tokens.
- Maximum context we need today: 16k tokens for reconciliation (we keep up to last 6 statements + metadata). Policy QA: 6k tokens.
- Retention: request-level PII must be redacted within 24 hours; we can accept caching of non-PII prefixes for 72 hours.

I attached clearledger_token_profile.csv with per-endpoint samples. Expect a couple of long outliers in reconciliation where prompts spike to 28k tokens; we flag those as 'archival' and they can be routed to an offline batch flow.

Cheers,
Ethan Cho
Head of Product Ops, ClearLedger
ethan@clearledger.com

Attachment: clearledger_token_profile.csv (CSV, 14KB)

Thanks Ethan — the numbers are clear and the outliers make sense. Quick internal notes and questions for sizing: 

1) Since they have steady ~12/min and short peaks to 75/min, a single 4-GPU Dedicated pool with dynamic burst should cover initial 6–8 week runway if we pick an optimized 70B-quant profile or a mid-size 30B with aggressive KV caching.
2) The 16k context for reconcile pushes us to prefer models with extended context support; options: (a) Proprietary Redwood-verified LLM-CTX-16k (quantized), (b) open-weights FalconX-40B-16k (FP16), (c) MPT-30B-extended (int8). We should avoid baseline 8k context models unless we plan to rewrite prompts to fetch summaries.
3) For PII constraints: because they require redaction within 24h, we need a policy to segregate redacted payloads from cache. Recommend setting prefix-caching only for non-PII routes and enabling eviction at 72h.

Action for Aditya: I’ll draft the model shortlist and a 4-week cost/latency table. Can you confirm whether ClearLedger expects synchronous SLAs for the archival long outliers or if those can be queued?

—Monica

Main ask: can you push an option that keeps per-call latency < 450ms p50 for the reconciliation happy path? That’s a product requirement we have for the live UI.

Team — thanks for the fast responses. Attached is the short triage doc and our recommended runway. Highlights: 

- Shortlist (3 variants):
  1) Redwood-CTX-16k-quant (recommended) — best latency/cost balance; p50 ~320ms on our 4xA10 profile at typical token mix; supports 16k natively.
  2) FalconX-40B-fp16 — stronger long-form coherence for complex reconciliations but ~1.6x higher cost; p50 ~480ms.
  3) MPT-30B-int8-extended — lowest cost option with good tail performance, but lower raw quality on legal/financial language.

- Routing policy: default to Redwood-CTX for synchronous UI calls (aim p50 <450ms), route large/archival >16k to async batch queue.
- Cache & retention: enable prefix caching for /policy-check and non-PII prefixes on /reconcile, TTL=72h; ensure redaction pipeline strips PII before any cache write.
- Runway sizing: initial Dedicated pool = 4 GPUs (A10-class); expected steady utilization ~35% with the shortlist; we forecast headroom for 12–18 months if they adopt prefix caching and default to 16k quant model.

Attachments: redwood_model-triage-notes.pdf (PDF, 36KB), runway-hourly-loads.xlsx (XLSX, 18KB)

Next steps: Monica will finalize the short doc and I’ll propose the Dedicated purchase order + kickoff calendar invite. Marissa — can you own the PO and SLA tickler?

Thanks,
